content.title: About
content.content: The whole wheat roll is a soft bun made from whole grain wheat flour. It has a subtle nutty flavor, a dense yet airy texture, and the characteristic aroma of fresh bread. It works well for breakfast, snacks, or as a base for sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain flour retains the bran and germ, making the roll more nutritious than white bread.
Traditionally these rolls were baked across Europe as a staple of daily meals.
Proper dough fermentation preserves natural flavors and improves digestibility.
The roll is often used as a base for open‑face sandwiches with vegetables and lean protein.
Its fiber content helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and maintains a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole grain flour provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white bread, the whole wheat roll raises blood sugar more slowly.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Beneficial fats and antioxidants in whole grains help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten intolerance should avoid the roll.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Those monitoring carb intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties are salted; choose unsalted versions if you have hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the whole wheat roll fresh, toasted, or as a sandwich base with lean meat, fish, vegetables, or hummus. It pairs well with low‑fat cheeses and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the roll in a paper bag or container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Warm in the oven or toaster before serving.
